title: What If the Dinosaur Asteroid Had Hit Somewhere Else?
topic: What if the dinosaur-killing asteroid had hit somewhere else? (Chicxulub, Kaiho & Oshima 2017)
mechanism: The Chicxulub asteroid struck a shallow sea on rock rich in sulfur and hydrocarbons; the blast lofted dust, sulfate and (some scientists add) soot from the burning oil, which dimmed the sun and froze the planet. Kaiho and Oshima's 2017 map and model say only about 13 % of Earth's surface has rock oily enough to make that much soot, so almost anywhere else the cooling would have been far milder; other scientists say the dust and sulfur alone were enough.

beats.hook: The asteroid that killed the giant dinosaurs may have hit one of the unluckiest spots on Earth: one push through the Cretaceous valley onto the T. rex while a bright streak crosses the sky.
beats.but: Sixty-six million years ago a rock six miles wide or more slams into what is now Mexico; the dinosaur asks why the sky is so bright.
beats.then: It lands in a shallow sea on rock packed with sulfur and buried oil (the cut-away seabed with SULFUR and OIL).
beats.conflict: Dust, sulfur and soot darken the sky, the planet goes cold; plants, plant eaters and meat eaters die; three quarters of species vanish.
beats.pivot: You see ... (the blast flung dust and sulfur high; soot from the burning oil). Then the 2017 globe: the oily rock covers only about 13 % of the surface; anywhere in the other 87 % their model's cooling is far milder.
beats.so: So the giant dinosaurs might have made it through; other scientists say the dust and sulfur alone were enough; nobody can rerun the test. Our tiny furry ancestors got the planet, grew and spread.
beats.closing: Today one of their descendants is watching this video. Unlucky spot for the dinosaurs. Lucky for you.

seed.what: The little furry mammal peeking from its burrow under the ferns (the survivor the ending depends on), and the OIL seam under the seabed
